CONTEXT. This is the 1852 fragment on the boundary values of the elliptic modular functions. It was published posthumously in Riemann's Werke as XXVIII, 'Fragmente über die Grenzfälle der elliptischen Modulfunctionen', with Dedekind's commentary. Here q is Jacobi's nome. The formulas use theta functions: k = θ2²/θ3², k' = θ4²/θ3², 2K/π = θ3², 2kK/π = θ2², 2k'K/π = θ4², 2√k'K/π = θ3θ4. Riemann puts q = e^{ix} and studies what the q-integrals ∫_0^q f(q) dq/q tend to as q approaches the unit circle radially. Riemann's ((y)) is the signed distance from y to the nearest integer, set to 0 at half-integers; this is the modern sawtooth function ((y)).

(A) END OF THE BRACKETED PROOF FROM THE PREVIOUS PAGE (formula 62, n even).
- Take x/2π = m/n with gcd(m,n)=1, so m is odd.
- Put q = ρ e^{2πim/n} and q0 = e^{2πim/n}.
- For odd p, q^{pn/2} = -ρ^{pn/2}. So the singular part (sign)·(16/n²) Σ_{p odd} log(1+q^{pn/2})/p² becomes (sign)·(16/n²) Σ_{p odd} log(1-ρ^{pn/2})/p².
- Next, log((q0-q)/(q0+q)) = log((1-ρ)/(1+ρ)), which is ~ log((1-ρ)/2) in the limit.
- Also (1-ρ^{pn/2})/(1-ρ) → pn/2.
- So log(1-ρ^{pn/2}) = log(1-ρ) + log(pn/2) + o(1).
- Using Σ_{p odd} 1/p² = π²/8 [my filling]: (16/n²)Σ_{p odd}[log(1-ρ) + log n - log 2 + log p]/p² = (2π²/n²)[log((q0-q)/(q0+q)) + log n + (8/π²)Σ_{p odd} log p/p²] + o(1).
- This is exactly the formula stated on the previous page.

(B) FORMULAS 63–68. Each comes from a Lambert-series expansion integrated termwise against dq/q, then evaluated at q = e^{ix}. Two evaluation rules are used:
- log(1+e^{iθ}) = ½log(4cos²(θ/2)) + iπ((θ/2π)).
- log(1-e^{iθ}) = ½log(4sin²(θ/2)) + iπ((θ/2π+½)).

63. -log k' = 4Σ_{j odd}[log(1+q^j) - log(1-q^j)] = 8Σ_{j,m odd} q^{jm}/m.
- Integrating: ∫_0^q (-log k') dq/q = Σ_{j odd}(4/j²) log((1+q^j)/(1-q^j)).
- At q = e^{ix} the real part is Σ_{j odd>0}(-2/j²) log tg²(jx/2) = -Σ_{p odd, -∞..∞} log tg²(px/2)/p².
- The imaginary part is Σ (4π/j²){((jx/2π)) - ((jx/2π+½))}.

64. log(2K/π) = Σ_{p odd}(4/p) q^p/(1+q^p).
- Hence ∫ = Σ_{p odd}(4/p²) log(1+q^p) = Σ_{p odd>0}(2/p²) log 4cos²(px/2) + i Σ (4π/p²)((px/2π)).

65. 2K/π - 1 = 4Σ_{p odd}(-1)^{(p-1)/2} q^p/(1-q^p).
- Hence ∫ = -4Σ_{p odd}(-1)^{(p-1)/2} log(1-q^p)/p.
- Real part: -2log4sin²(x/2) + (2/3)log4sin²(3x/2) - ...
- Imaginary part: -4π((x/2π+½)) + (4π/3)((3x/2π+½)) - ...
- Second form: the same series regrouped as 4Σ_{n≥1} q^n/(1+q^{2n}), which gives ∫ = 4Σ_n arctan(q^n)/n.
- Here arctan z = (1/2i) log((1+iz)/(1-iz)) and (1+ie^{iθ})/(1-ie^{iθ}) = i·cot((2θ+π)/4).
- This yields Σ_n (i/n) log tg²((2nx+π)/4) + Σ_n (2π/n){((nx/2π+¼)) - ((nx/2π+¾))}.
- The roles of real and imaginary parts are thus swapped between the two expansions.

66. 2kK/π = θ2² = 4Σ_{p odd} q^{p/2}/(1+q^p).
- Regrouped: ∫ = 4Σ_{j odd}(-1)^{(j-1)/2}(1/j) log((1+q^{j/2})/(1-q^{j/2})).
- This gives -2log tg²(x/4) + (2/3)log tg²(3x/4) - ... + 4πi Σ ±(1/j){((jx/4π)) - ((jx/4π+½))}.
- Alternatively: ∫ = Σ_{p odd}(8/p) arctan(q^{p/2}) = Σ (2i/p) log tg²((px+π)/4) + Σ (4π/p){((px/4π+¼)) - ((px/4π+¾))}.

67. θ4²(q) = θ3²(-q), i.e. replace x by x+π in 65.
- 2k'K/π - 1 = -4Σ_{p odd}(-1)^{(p-1)/2} q^p/(1+q^p), so ∫ = -4Σ(-1)^{(p-1)/2} log(1+q^p)/p.
- In the second form the terms with odd n change sign, because tg(α+nπ/2) = -cot α for odd n.

68. θ3(q)θ4(q) = θ4(q²)². So 68 is 67 with q→q², i.e. x→2x, with all coefficients halved.

(C) RATIONAL POINTS IN 65. Take x = 2πm/n. The imaginary part of 65 is -4π Σ_{p odd}(-1)^{(p-1)/2}((pm/n+½))/p. Group p by residues:
- n even: p ↦ p+ns (s ≥ 0), with sign factor (-1)^{ns/2}.
- n odd: period 2n, p ↦ p+2ns, with sign factor (-1)^s.
- If n ≢ 0 mod 4, the outer series in s alternates, so it converges.
- If n ≡ 0 mod 4, all signs agree and Σ_s 1/(p+ns) diverges, unless the residue sum vanishes.
- So Riemann's claim is: finite unless n ≡ 0 mod 4.
- The page closes by announcing the analogous residue-class decomposition for the real parts of 63 and 64; these are carried out on the next page.
errors: No substantive mathematical error found. Formulas 63–68 check out coefficient by coefficient against the theta and Lambert expansions, including signs and the sawtooth (( )) terms.

All the boundary series (e.g. Σ log tg²(px/2)/p²) converge only conditionally or not at all for irrational x/2π. They are meaningful only via the Abel-type limit lemma on the previous/next page, which Riemann invokes. The termwise passage to |q| = 1 is therefore justified only under that lemma.
Divergence claim for n ≡ 0 mod 4 in 65: strictly, divergence needs Σ_{p odd<n}(-1)^{(p-1)/2}((pm/n+½)) ≠ 0. Riemann asserts this without proof. It holds e.g. for n=4, m=1, where the sum is -1/2.
The order of terms in the second line of 65 is jumbled: the 2π/3 term is written before the 2π and 2π/2 terms. This is cosmetic.

The sign factor in the limit bracket is written (-1)^{m/2} on the previous page, but m is odd there. The sign arising from (-1)^N at N = pn/2 with p odd is (-1)^{n/2}. Probably a slip in one of the two places.

results.what: Asymptotic of the singular part at a rational boundary point (n even) for ∫(log k - log 4√q)dq/q, involving log((q0-q)/(q0+q)) + log n + (8/π²)Σ_{p odd} log p/p²
results.modern_name: Boundary asymptotics of log of modular forms / Eichler-type integrals at cusps
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Werke XXVIII, 1852 fragment), commented by Dedekind 1876/1892

results.what: Integrated logarithmic and Lambert series for -log k', log(2K/π), 2K/π-1, 2kK/π, 2k'K/π-1, 2√k'K/π-1, evaluated on |q|=1 in terms of log|sin|, log|cos|, log|tan| and the sawtooth ((x))
results.modern_name: Boundary values of Eichler integrals of weight-1 theta products; Lambert-series and arctan expansions of θ2², θ3², θ4²

results.what: At x = 2πm/n, splitting into residue classes mod n or 2n, with the convergence criterion n ≢ 0 mod 4; these finite sums of sawtooth functions are the germ of Dedekind sums
results.modern_name: Dedekind-sum-type finite sums Σ((pm/n)) …, behaviour of theta functions at cusps
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind (1892 commentary on this very fragment)

deep.surprise_reason: This page belongs to the 1852 fragment on limiting cases of elliptic modular functions, published in Riemann's Werke (XXVIII) with Dedekind's commentary, which famously led to Dedekind sums. Its contents are already attributed to Riemann in the literature.

transcription_corrections: 'log lg' throughout (63, 65–68) should read 'log tg' (logarithm of tangent).
In the limit bracket the prefactor is 16/n² (as on the previous page), not 16/π²; the sign exponent appears as n/2 here versus m/2 on the previous page.
In the limit bracket the sum is over odd p only (p 'numerus impar'), not over all p from 1 to ∞.
In 65 the term ordering on the second line is jumbled in the transcription; the image has the 2π(…), 2π/2(…), 2π/3(…) terms in natural order across two lines.
